1.explanation: parser-markdown.js is responsible for turning your Markdown text (including raw HTML blocks) into an AST, and it must tag HTML blocks correctly for the printer. printer-markdown.js contains the logic that takes that AST and re-serializes it—specifically it handles list indentation and how raw HTML (html node) is printed under a list item. The current code there does not preserve the original indentation for HTML blocks in lists, causing the indent to grow on each format. Adjusting these two files will allow us to detect an html node inside a list and print it with the correct fixed indent rather than incrementing it every save.
1.bug_scenario:
When you put a raw HTML table under a numbered list in a Markdown file and have “format on save” enabled in VS Code (using Prettier), each time you save the file Prettier re-indents the entire block one more level to the right. The GIF shows a simple list item “1.” containing an indented
